Slot quality: The single slot correctly captures name, age band (12m–4y), days/times/dates (Tues & Thurs, 9:30–11:00 a.m., Sept 8–Dec 11), and honestly handles the missing fee by pointing to the front desk / phone, all attributed to the preschool-play page. Critically, it does NOT borrow the $185 birthday-party figure from the room-rentals page — exactly the fabrication watchFor flags. Price is marked as not posted on this page, which is accurate (the page says "see fee schedule at front desk or call"), and since pageEvidence is page_has_schedule this is correct: the page was read, it had a schedule but no numeric price, so "fee not listed on this page" is earned and honest.

Message quality: Leads with the programme name and venue. All session facts (days, times, date range) are present and correct. Attributes with "their site says." Price is handled correctly — "I couldn't pin down the price or registration from their page" is first-person, which is appropriate here because the page WAS read and HAS a schedule but the price simply isn't numeric on the page (it redirects to the front desk). This phrasing is slightly imprecise (it sounds like Hale failed rather than that the page directs elsewhere), but it is not an unearned negative claim and does not misreport a schedule as "not posted."

Watch=true and the message closes with "I'll keep watching and text you once those are confirmed" — first-person commitment present, as required.

No rental figure injected. No fabricated price. No question asked. No link. Two sentences, plain ASCII. Registration not stated on the page and not dropped from the message (there was nothing to carry). The slot notes "Not stated on this page" for registration, which is accurate and correctly carried through.

Minor imperfection: "I couldn't pin down the price or registration from their page" slightly frames this as Hale's failure rather than the page's redirect, but it does not assert "not posted yet" (which would require page_has_no_schedule), and it is first-person as required. This is a minor phrasing quibble, not a scoring fault under the rubric. Overall this is a strong, accurate, honest pass.
